chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'What is the reward for one who visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) as a visitor, knowing his right, neither arrogant nor disdainful?' He replied, 'A thousand purified Hajj and a thousand purified Umrah are recorded for him. And if he were among the wretched, he would be recorded among the blissful, and he would continuously be immersed in the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.) with humility?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this tradition highlighting the transformative power of Ziyarat al-Husayn, where the visitor's spiritual state is elevated regardless of their prior destiny. This reward of a thousand purified Hajj and Umrah underscores the Imam's role as a conduit of divine mercy, a concept deeply rooted in Shia theology regarding the intercession and spiritual authority of the Ahl al-Bayt.
